scenario_description:
Objective: Add an optional public ballot-tracking lookup mini-demo to Monday's quick-reference huddle.
Emerging Need: A no-cost demo monitor opening appears while the huddle is tentative; later volunteer confusion and a confirmed room with projection make the add-on useful.
Decision Context: Stored huddle procedure supplies the standard request route, canned demo record, live-data limits, and cutoff needed to judge a proportional hold.
Consequence: Timely coordination could make volunteers' public-resource explanations clearer; after the monitor roster locks, the huddle simply proceeds with its ordinary discussion notes.

parameter.title: Volunteer Services Quick-Reference Huddle
parameter.description: Tentative internal huddle to compare neutral answers for common public-resource questions before next week's service tables.

parameter.subject: Public lookup demo monitor available for one volunteer huddle
parameter.body: The Public Tools unit can support one no-cost read-only demo monitor for a confirmed volunteer huddle next week. Use the standard mini-demo procedure if a session becomes firm enough for the add-on; otherwise no response is needed.

parameter.content: Morning desk note: two newer volunteers were unsure how to describe the county's public ballot-tracking lookup without drifting into case-specific advice. They said seeing the official public page once would make the huddle more useful if it happens.

parameter.title: Volunteer Services Quick-Reference Huddle
parameter.description: Confirmed internal huddle to compare neutral answers for common public-resource questions; room includes a projector and staff-managed display cart.

parameter.subject: Demo monitor roster locked for July 6 huddles
parameter.body: The read-only public-tools demo monitor roster for Monday sessions is now locked, and the remaining display cart has been assigned. Huddles may still use their regular discussion notes without the live public-page demonstration.
